metadata.name: Stroke (10-year)

sources.citation: Global Burden of Disease Study 2019 - Stroke
American Heart Association/American Stroke Association Guidelines (2021)

metadata.description: Cerebrovascular accident - blockage or rupture of blood vessels in the brain

caseFatality10yr.basis: Perth Community Stroke Study: 79% (95% CI 74-84%) dead within 10 years of first-ever stroke
caseFatality10yr.citation: Hardie K, Hankey GJ, Jamrozik K, Broadhurst RJ, Anderson C. Ten-year risk of first recurrent stroke and disability after first-ever stroke. Stroke. 2003;34(8):1842-1846
caseFatality10yr.notes: All-cause mortality among the diagnosed (annual death rate of survivors 2.3x matched population); includes background mortality

curves.source: Global Burden of Disease Study 2019 (US-specific stroke incidence rates)
curves.notes: Age-standardized incidence declining 20-30% since 1990 but absolute cases rising; male rates higher than females across ages 50+; derived from 29-year US data showing exponential increase with age.

curves.source: Global Burden of Disease Study 2019 (US-specific stroke incidence rates)
curves.notes: Female rates lower than males but increasing in <50s; 2019 US estimates: ~460k incident strokes, 2/3 ischemic.

riskFactors.name: Hypertension
riskFactors.citation: Blood Pressure and Stroke (Prospective Studies Collaboration meta-analysis)
riskFactors.notes: Per 10 mmHg higher SBP: ~33% higher stroke risk; log-linear from 115 mmHg; consistent across subtypes.

riskFactors.name: Diabetes
riskFactors.citation: Global Burden of Disease Stroke Risk Factors 1990-2019
riskFactors.notes: Diabetes attributable fraction ~10-15% strokes; HR ~2.0 in meta-analyses (e.g., Framingham-derived).

riskFactors.name: Current Smoking
riskFactors.notes: Current: HR~2.0, former: HR~1.3 vs never; dose-response with pack-years.

riskFactors.name: Atrial Fibrillation
riskFactors.citation: Atrial fibrillation burden and stroke risk: systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis
riskFactors.notes: AF burden >5 min: adjusted RR=2.49 (95% CI 1.79-3.47); dose-response: 2% increased risk per hour; aligns with ~5.0 HR in CHA2DS2-VASc scoring.

riskFactors.name: History of Cardiovascular Disease
riskFactors.citation: Wolf PA, Abbott RD, Kannel WB. Atrial fibrillation as an independent risk factor for stroke: the Framingham Study. Stroke. 1991;22(8):983-988
riskFactors.notes: Framingham: age-adjusted stroke incidence roughly doubled with coronary heart disease; 1.6 is a conservative adjusted estimate (CHARLS 2025: HR 1.96, 1.55-2.48).

riskFactors.name: Prior Stroke or TIA
riskFactors.citation: Lioutas VA, et al. Incidence of Transient Ischemic Attack and Association With Long-term Risk of Stroke. JAMA. 2021;325(4):373-381
riskFactors.notes: Framingham: fully adjusted 10-year stroke HR after TIA 4.37 (3.30-5.71); cumulative post-TIA stroke risk 19.8% at 10 years in 38-study meta-analysis.

riskFactors.name: HDL Cholesterol (Protective)
riskFactors.citation: Dose-Response Association Between High-Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol and Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Prospective Cohort Studies. Prev Chronic Dis. 2021;18:E100
riskFactors.notes: Total stroke RR 0.82 (0.76-0.89) per 1 mmol/L (38.7 mg/dL) higher HDL (62 cohorts, 900,501 participants). Caveat: high HDL is associated with INCREASED intracerebral hemorrhage (RR 1.21).

riskFactors.name: Body Mass Index
riskFactors.citation: Strazzullo P, et al. Excess body weight and incidence of stroke: meta-analysis of prospective studies with 2 million participants. Stroke. 2010;41(5):e418-e426
riskFactors.notes: Ischemic stroke: overweight RR 1.22 (1.05-1.41), obese RR 1.64 (1.36-1.99); values map the pooled estimates conservatively across the BMI range.
